newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE CHANGED ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES LITTLE CHANGED ON FRIDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable at their previous levels on Friday, apparently disregarding a slight drop in the benchmark treasury bill rate at Thursday's weekly tender.

Dealers said the tender rate came to 17.80 percent on Thursday from 17.88 percent the previous week, but on Friday discount houses were selling treasury bills in the market unchanged at 17.65 percent.
"The market is fairly active today compared to yesterday and we're expecting a number of maturities," one dealer commented.
Bankers acceptance bills were being bought at a steady 18.50 percent but were selling easier at 17.70 percent compared to 18 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were stable at 19 and 18.25 percent (buying and selling respectively) and call money remained at 18.50 percent.

Reserve Bank figures indicated a market shortage of Z$17 million at the close of Thursday trade, compared to a previous Z$212.1 million surplus. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 28/9--
